topics.name: Choosing Workflows, Agents and Frameworks
topics.description: Pick between workflows and agents, and between create_agent, LangGraph and Deep Agents.
notes: ## 工作流 vs Agent
- Workflow：代码路径预先确定，按固定顺序执行。
- Agent：动态决定自己的流程和工具使用，适合问题与解法不可预测的场景。
- 两者都可以在 LangGraph 中实现，也可以在同一张图里混用确定性步骤和 agentic 步骤。
## 常见 workflow 模式
- Prompt chaining：每次 LLM 调用处理上一次的输出，适合可拆成可验证小步骤的任务。
- Parallelization：并行运行子任务（提速）或重复运行同一任务（提高置信度）。
- Routing：先对输入分类，再路由到专门的处理流程。
- Orchestrator-worker：子任务无法预先定义时，由 orchestrator 拆分、worker 执行、最后综合；LangGraph 用 Send API 动态创建 worker。
- Evaluator-optimizer：一个 LLM 生成，另一个评估并给反馈，循环直到满足标准。
## 三层选择
- LangChain create_agent：高度可定制的 agent harness，用 middleware 逐步添加能力。
- LangGraph：低层编排框架和运行时，适合组合确定性与 agentic 工作流，提供持久化、流式、human-in-the-loop。
- Deep Agents：开箱即用的 harness，内置上下文压缩、虚拟文件系统、subagent、规划等；构建于 LangChain agents 之上，运行在 LangGraph 上。
- LangSmith：无论用哪一层，都用它来 trace、调试和评估。
```python
from langchain.agents import create_agent
agent = create_agent(model="gpt-5.5", tools=[get_weather], system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant")

topics.name: Thinking in LangGraph Methodology
topics.description: Break a process into nodes, classify step types, design raw state and choose error strategies.
notes: ## 五步法
- 1) 把流程拆成离散步骤，每一步成为一个 node，再画出它们的连接。
- 2) 判断每一步的类型以及它需要的上下文。
- 3) 设计 state。
- 4) 实现 node（接收 state，返回更新）。
- 5) 连线并用 checkpointer 编译。
## 四种 node 类型
- LLM step：理解、分析、生成文本或做推理决策。
- Data step：从外部数据源检索信息，可配合重试和缓存。
- Action step：执行外部动作（发送邮件、建工单），重试要谨慎，不应缓存。
- User input step：需要人工介入，用 interrupt() 暂停。
## State 设计
- 需要跨步骤保留的数据才放进 state；能由其他数据推导的就不要存。
- State 存原始数据，不存格式化好的 prompt；在 node 内按需格式化。
## 错误处理策略
- 临时错误（网络、限流）：RetryPolicy 自动重试。
- LLM 可恢复错误（工具失败、解析问题）：把错误写进 state 并回到 LLM。
- 用户可修复错误（缺少信息）：interrupt() 暂停等待输入。
- 意外错误：让它抛出，便于调试。
```python
workflow.add_node("search_documentation", search_documentation,
retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, initial_interval=1.0))

topics.name: Context Engineering and Agent Assembly
topics.description: Control what the model sees using state, store, runtime context and middleware.
notes: ## 为什么需要 context engineering
- Agent 失败通常有两个原因：模型能力不足，或没有把「正确的上下文」交给模型；后者更常见。
- Context engineering：以正确的格式提供正确的信息和工具，让 LLM 完成任务。
## 三类上下文
- Model context（瞬时）：system prompt、messages、tools、model、response format。
- Tool context（持久）：工具读写 state、store、runtime context。
- Life-cycle context（持久）：模型调用与工具调用之间的摘要、护栏、日志等。
## 三种数据源
- Runtime Context：静态配置，对话范围，如 user ID、权限、API key。
- State：短期记忆，对话范围，如当前 messages、工具结果。
- Store：长期记忆，跨对话，如用户偏好。
## 实现方式：middleware
- wrap_model_call 用 request.override(...) 修改 messages、tools、model 或 response_format，只影响单次调用（瞬时）。
- SummarizationMiddleware 会永久用摘要替换旧消息；ContextEditingMiddleware 清理旧的工具输出。
- 工具太多会让模型困惑，可动态筛选或用 LLMToolSelectorMiddleware。
- 最佳实践：先从静态 prompt 和工具开始，每次只增加一个动态功能，并监控 token 与延迟。
```python
SummarizationMiddleware(model="gpt-5.4-mini", trigger=("tokens", 4000), keep=("messages", 20))

topics.name: Evaluation, Safeguards and Deployment Readiness
topics.description: Pre-release gates: evals, trace metadata, approvals, limits and langgraph.json.
notes: ## 评估闸门
- Offline evaluation：发布前在 dataset 上测试，用于基准对比、回归测试、单元测试。
- Online evaluation：发布后在生产 run 与 thread 上监控质量，没有参考答案。
- 先手工整理 10-20 个高质量样例定义「好」的标准；上线后可把真实 trace 转成样例。
- 评估指标可转成测试：回归测试可要求新版本在关键指标上优于基线。
## 观测
- 设置 LANGSMITH_TRACING=true 与 API key 开启 trace。
- Tags 是字符串标签；metadata 是键值字典，可记录环境、用户或内部关联 ID。
- 把 LANGSMITH_REVISION_ID 设为 git commit，可按 revision_id 过滤某次提交的 trace。
## 风险控制
- HumanInTheLoopMiddleware 对高风险工具暂停，允许 approve / edit / reject，且需要 checkpointer。
- interrupt() 要放在 node 最前面，因为它之前的代码在恢复时会重新执行。
- ModelCallLimitMiddleware / ToolCallLimitMiddleware 限制调用次数，防止失控循环和过高成本。
## 部署配置
- langgraph.json 指定 dependencies、graphs、env。
- graphs 的值形如 ./your_package/your_file.py:agent，即文件路径加变量名。
- 本地用 env 指向 .env；生产环境通常在部署环境里配置环境变量。
```json
{"dependencies": ["langchain_openai", "./your_package"],
"graphs": {"my_agent": "./your_package/your_file.py:agent"}, "env": "./.env"}

questions.title: According to the LangGraph docs, what is the main difference between a workflow and an agent?

options.text: Workflows always use tools, agents never do
Agents have predetermined code paths, workflows decide their own steps
Workflows have predetermined code paths, agents define their own process and tool usage
Workflows cannot call an LLM, agents can

questions.explanation: Workflows follow code paths fixed in advance, while agents are dynamic and choose their own process and tools. Option B reverses the two definitions.

questions.title: Which product is described as the low-level orchestration framework for combining deterministic and agentic workflows?

options.text: LangGraph
LangChain create_agent
Deep Agents
LangSmith tracing

questions.explanation: The docs recommend LangGraph for advanced needs that mix deterministic and agentic steps. create_agent is a higher-level configurable harness, and LangSmith is for tracing and evaluation.

questions.title: You want a batteries-included harness with context compression, a virtual filesystem and subagents. Which option do the docs point to?

options.text: A hand-built LangGraph StateGraph with no prebuilt components
LangSmith tracing
A bare create_agent call with no middleware
Deep Agents

questions.explanation: Deep Agents is the harness that adds context management, a virtual filesystem and subagent delegation on top of LangChain and LangGraph. create_agent is a minimal harness you extend yourself.

questions.title: Which are named workflow patterns in the LangGraph 'Workflows and agents' guide?

options.text: Prompt chaining
Routing
Hierarchical sharding
Evaluator-optimizer

questions.explanation: The guide covers prompt chaining, parallelization, routing, orchestrator-worker and evaluator-optimizer. Hierarchical sharding is not one of them.

questions.title: What does assign_workers do in this orchestrator-worker graph?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langgraph.types import Send

def assign_workers(state: State):
    return [Send("llm_call", {"section": s}) for s in state["sections"]]

builder.add_conditional_edges("orchestrator", assign_workers, ["llm_call"])

options.text: Runs llm_call once with the whole list of sections
Creates one llm_call worker per section at run time, each with its own input
Routes the graph straight to END
Adds exactly three fixed parallel edges when the graph is built

questions.explanation: The Send API dynamically creates a worker per item and sends each its own input, so the number of workers is not fixed at build time.

questions.title: A workflow must update install instructions in an unknown number of documents, so the subtasks cannot be predefined. Which pattern fits best?

options.text: Parallelization with a fixed set of branches
Prompt chaining with a fixed number of calls
Routing to a single specialized path
Orchestrator-worker, where an orchestrator plans subtasks and delegates them to workers

questions.explanation: Orchestrator-worker is used when subtasks cannot be predefined the way they can with parallelization. The orchestrator breaks the task down, delegates it and synthesizes the results.

questions.title: get_user_info needs state["user_id"], but it is not available inside the tool. Why?

options.text: Tools can never read graph state
Only a Store can hold a user_id
The @tool decorator needs parse_docstring=True
The ToolNode is invoked with only messages, so other state keys are not exposed; pass the full state

questions.explanation: Tools can only access the state values passed to the ToolNode, and passing only the messages exposes only messages. Invoking it with the full state exposes custom fields such as user_id.

questions.title: What is the first step of the 'Thinking in LangGraph' method?

options.text: Map the workflow into discrete steps, each of which becomes a node
Compile the graph with a checkpointer
Write the final prompt templates
Choose a deployment platform

questions.explanation: Step 1 is to identify the distinct steps of the process; each becomes a node and you sketch how they connect. Compiling with a checkpointer is the last step.

questions.title: Which are the node (step) types the guide uses to classify what each step does?

options.text: LLM steps
Data steps
Action steps
User input steps
Deployment steps

questions.explanation: The guide classifies steps as LLM, data, action or user input steps. Deployment is not a step type.

questions.title: What should the graph state store, according to the guide?

options.text: Fully formatted prompt strings ready to send to the model
Only the final answer shown to the user
Raw data; format the prompt inside each node when needed
Every value that can be derived from other data

questions.explanation: Keeping state raw lets different nodes format the same data differently and lets you change templates without changing the schema. Derivable data should be computed, not stored.

questions.title: A node cannot continue because the customer's account ID is missing. Which error-handling strategy does the guide recommend?

options.text: Let the exception bubble up for debugging
Pause with interrupt() and collect the missing information from the user
Add a RetryPolicy with exponential backoff
Store the error in state and loop back to the LLM

questions.explanation: Missing information is a user-fixable error, which is handled by pausing with interrupt(). Retrying will not conjure the missing ID.

questions.title: Fill in the blank so that this node is retried automatically on transient failures.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langgraph.types import RetryPolicy

workflow.add_node(
    "search_documentation",
    search_documentation,
    ______=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, initial_interval=1.0),
)

options.text: on_error
retry
retry_policy
policy

questions.explanation: add_node accepts a retry_policy argument for transient errors such as network issues and rate limits. The other names are not parameters shown in the docs.

questions.title: What does this node do when run_tool raises ToolError versus any other exception?

options.text: ToolError is written to state and sent back to the agent so the LLM can adjust; other exceptions bubble up
Both kinds are swallowed and the graph ends
ToolError pauses the graph for a human; other exceptions are retried
Both kinds are written to state and routed back to the agent

questions.explanation: ToolError is an LLM-recoverable error: it is stored in state and the graph loops back so the model can see it. The bare raise lets unexpected errors surface for debugging.

questions.title: Why can splitting a workflow into smaller nodes reduce repeated work after a failure?

options.text: Smaller nodes make the LLM faster
Checkpoints are created at node boundaries, and a resumed run restarts from the beginning of the node where it stopped
Smaller nodes disable checkpointing so nothing is saved
The graph skips every node that already ran in any previous thread

questions.explanation: Persistence checkpoints at node boundaries, so a large node must be re-executed from its start. The docs note this is a trade-off against observability and isolation, not a speed-up of the LLM.

questions.title: According to the context engineering guide, what most often makes agents unreliable?

options.text: The right context was not passed to the LLM
Python is too slow
Tools return too few characters
The system prompt is always too short

questions.explanation: The guide says LLMs fail either because the model is not capable enough or because the right context was not passed, and more often it is the second reason.

questions.title: Which of these are part of 'model context' that you can control for each model call?

options.text: System prompt
Message history
Response format
Docker base image

questions.explanation: Model context covers instructions, messages, tools, the model itself and the response format. The container image is not part of what goes into a model call.

questions.title: Which approach permanently replaces old messages in state with a summary for all future turns?

options.text: A wrap_model_call middleware that uses request.override(messages=...)
A dynamic_prompt middleware
SummarizationMiddleware
Filtering request.tools

questions.explanation: SummarizationMiddleware is a life-cycle pattern that persistently updates state. Changes made with wrap_model_call overrides are transient and affect only that single model call.

questions.title: Complete the middleware so that the model only sees read-only tools for this call.

options.text: replace
set
update
override

questions.explanation: The docs use request.override(...) to change tools, messages, model or response_format for the current call. The other methods are not shown in the guide.

questions.title: What happens once the conversation exceeds 4000 tokens with this configuration?
questions.codeSnippet:
agent = create_agent(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    tools=[...],
    middleware=[
        SummarizationMiddleware(
            model="gpt-5.4-mini",
            trigger=("tokens", 4000),
            keep=("messages", 20),
        ),
    ],
)

options.text: The agent raises an error and stops
Only the 20 oldest messages are kept
Older messages are summarized by gpt-5.4-mini and the 20 most recent messages are kept
All messages are deleted without a summary

questions.explanation: trigger sets when summarization runs and keep sets how much recent context is preserved. Older messages are condensed by the separate summary model.

questions.title: When does this SummarizationMiddleware trigger?

options.text: Only when tokens >= 4000 AND messages >= 10
When either tokens >= 4000 OR messages >= 10
Never, because trigger must be a tuple
Only when exactly 4000 tokens are reached

questions.explanation: A single TriggerClause dict requires all of its thresholds to be met (AND). To express OR, pass a list of conditions instead.

questions.title: The agent has 10 tools, including one named search. At most how many tools can the main model see per call here?

options.text: 3 in total, including search
4: three selected tools plus search
1, only search

questions.explanation: Tools listed in always_include are added regardless of selection and do not count against max_tools. So up to three selected tools plus search reach the main model.

questions.title: In LangSmith, which trace attribute is a dictionary of key-value pairs, for example the environment or an internal correlation ID?

options.text: Tags
Metadata
Experiments
Datasets

questions.explanation: Metadata is a dictionary of key-value pairs, while tags are plain strings used to label a trace.

questions.title: Which does the langgraph.json configuration file specify?

options.text: Dependencies
Graphs
Environment variables
The sampling temperature of the model

questions.explanation: langgraph.json specifies the dependencies, graphs and environment variables of the application. Model parameters live in your code.

questions.title: In langgraph.json, what does the entry "my_agent": "./your_package/your_file.py:agent" under "graphs" mean?

options.text: The graph named my_agent is loaded from the variable agent in that file
The file is installed as a pip dependency
agent is an environment variable name
The text after the colon is a model name

questions.explanation: Each graph has a unique name and a path to either the compiled graph or a function that builds one, written as file path plus variable.

questions.title: Which statements about LangSmith offline and online evaluation are correct?

options.text: Offline evaluations run on dataset examples that can have reference outputs
Online evaluations target runs and threads from production traces
Online evaluators can compare outputs with dataset reference outputs
Offline evaluation suits regression testing before deployment

questions.explanation: Online evaluations work on live runs and have no reference outputs, so they cannot do reference-based comparison. Offline evaluations on datasets are meant for pre-deployment checks such as regression testing.

questions.title: Fill in the blank. Human-in-the-loop middleware needs this to keep state across the interruption.

options.text: InMemoryStore
SummarizationMiddleware
ToolNode
InMemorySaver

questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop requires a checkpointer, and InMemorySaver is the in-memory checkpointer used in the docs. InMemoryStore is long-term memory, not a checkpointer.

questions.title: With the default exit_behavior, what happens when the model requests a 4th search call in one run?
questions.codeSnippet:
agent = create_agent(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    tools=[search_tool, database_tool],
    middleware=[
        ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name="search", thread_limit=5, run_limit=3),
    ],
)

options.text: ToolCallLimitExceededError is raised immediately
The extra search call is blocked with an error message and the model can continue
Every tool is disabled for the rest of the thread
The run limit is ignored until the thread limit of 5 is reached

questions.explanation: The default exit_behavior is 'continue': exceeded calls are blocked with error messages while the model decides how to proceed. Raising an exception requires exit_behavior='error'.

questions.title: Reviewers report duplicate notifications after approving drafts. What is the bug?

options.text: interrupt() cannot receive a dictionary
The node must return a Command instead of a dict
send_notification runs before interrupt(), so it re-runs when the graph resumes; put interrupt() first
decision should be read from the checkpointer

questions.explanation: On resume the node restarts, so any code before interrupt() runs again. The docs say interrupt() should come first when combined with other operations in a node.
